thesis: The speakers argue that curing all disease by the end of the century requires fundamentally new tools to accelerate basic science rather than simply increasing funding for individual labs. They propose bridging the gap between biology and AI by building shared infrastructure, such as virtual cell models and open-source data, to enable scientists to test high-risk hypotheses in silico before conducting extensive wet lab work.
